title: Mini Project - Spatial
text:
A report completed as a “Mini Project” in STAT 452 - Correlated Data in the fall of 2025. This project examines how median household income and median age relate to home values across census tracts in Ramsey County, MN using spatial regression models that account for geographic dependence. The results show that higher-income and older-population areas tend to have higher home values, and a spatial error model (SAR) best captures the structure in the data by removing residual spatial autocorrelation.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure and Iris Fokam for Professor Brianna Heggeseth.


Check out the report!

title: Mini Project - Longitudinal
text:
A report completed as a “Mini Project” in STAT 452 - Correlated Data in the fall of 2025. This project uses a generalized estimating equation (GEE) model to study how cognitive training interventions in the ACTIVE study affect reasoning scores over time in older adults. The results show that both reasoning and other cognitive training groups improve performance relative to controls, with reasoning training having the strongest long-term positive effect.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure and Alicia Severiano Perez for Professor Brianna Heggeseth.


Check out the report!

title: STAT 212 Semester Project
text:
A project completed as the final project in STAT 212 - Intermediate Data Science in the fall of 2024. As a semester-long culmination of work, we collaborated with the Macalester Women’s Volleyball coaching staff to craft two main research questions: how can game statistics be used to predict the outcome of a game, and how have senior players (graduating class of 2025) improved over their time at Macalester. Our work is summarized and visualized in an interactive Shiny app, which can be accessed below.


This project was created by Katelyn McClure and Kynan Desouza-Chen.


Check out our Shiny app!

title: STAT 112 Final Group Project
text:
A project completed as the final project in STAT 112 - Introduction to Data Science in the spring of 2024. An introductory set of visualizations and tables that give insight into the different raw number and proportions of species classified as some level of threatened by the US National Park service. One of the main focuses of the assignment was the data cleaning process, which included the joining of a few separate datasets, creating new categorical variables for the numerous national park regions, and the removal of any missing data.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure, Megan Diller, and Sydney Stratton.


Check out our report and presentation!

title: Mini Project - Time Series
text:
A report completed as a “Mini Project” in STAT 452 - Correlated Data in the fall of 2025. This project analyzes electricity usage at Macalester’s Eco House using time series methods to identify long-term trends, seasonal patterns, and forecast future consumption. The results show a peak in usage around 2018 followed by a gradual decline, strong seasonal variation, and stable short-term dynamics captured well by an AR(2) model.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure and Lilabeth Sokolewicz for Professor Brianna Heggeseth.


Check out the report!

title: Bayesian Statistics Final Project
text:
A report completed as the final project in STAT 454 - Bayesian Statistics in the spring of 2026. This project applies Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) to simulated regression data to account for model uncertainty by averaging across many possible predictor combinations instead of selecting a single “best” model. The results show that BMA successfully identifies true predictors (\(x_1\) and \(x_3\)), filters out noise variables even in large model spaces, and produces accurate predictions while highlighting the usefulness of methods like Occam’s Window and MCMC for scalable model selection..


A capstone experience in Macalester’s Mathematics, Statistics, and Computer Science department is a year-long, culminating project in which students complete substantial independent work in a 400-level course and then develop it into a polished, public-facing presentation. The process includes a senior seminar focused on translating technical work into a clear narrative for general audiences, followed by a 15–20 minute talk at Capstone Days where students present their work in a department-wide mini-conference. Statistics majors are required to take two 400-level courses to graduate, but only need to present one capstone project during capstone days.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure and Isa Chen for Professor Taylor Okonek.


Check out the report and my final class presentation slide deck!

title: STEAM: Summer Research 2024
text:
Admixture mapping is important for identifying disease genes, especially in populations with mixed ancestry. In the summer of 2024, we worked on improving an R package, called STEAM, that finds a genome-wide significance threshold that can be used in admixture mapping. Our process started with reviewing how other researchers were utilizing STEAM in their own research projects, and then using this understanding to improve and debug the code. We also prioritized enhancing the usability of the STEAM package with new features and updated documentation in addition to making efforts to increase STEAM’s visibility as an R package. My primary focus was creating a vignette to serve as a guide for new users of the package.


This project was led by Dr. Kelsey Grinde with undergraduate research assistants Katelyn McClure, Sydney Ohr, and Tina Chen.


Check out our research poster and the STEAM R package!

title: STAT 155 Final Group Project
text:
A report completed as the final project in STAT 155 - Introduction to Statistical Modeling in the fall of 2023. An introductory analysis of the relationship between 9 different countries’ greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) and their gross domestic products (GDP). The report includes linear regression models that capture the relationship between GHG and GDP across our 3 different categories of countries: high, median, and low GDP.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure, Julia Brandfonbrener, Sam Fyle, and Lilabeth Sokolewicz.


Check out the report!

title: Bayesian Technical Report 2
text:
A report completed as a technical report in in STAT 454 - Bayesian Statistics in the spring of 2026. This project uses a Bayesian hierarchical logistic regression model to analyze whether using a Power Play in mixed doubles curling affects the U.S. team’s probability of winning a match.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure and Isa Chen for Professor Taylor Okonek.


Check out the report!

title: Capstone Project
text:
A report completed as the final project in STAT 452 - Correlated Data in the fall of 2025. A longitudinal analysis using GEE to estimate the impact of income, land value, and year to view trends in the presence of leisure venues (museums, sports venues, theaters, etc.) in the 7-county Twin Cities metro area of Minnesota.

title: Bayesian Technical Report 1
text:
A report completed as a technical report in in STAT 454 - Bayesian Statistics in the spring of 2026. This project uses a Bayesian model (Beta–Geometric framework) to estimate the probability of growing a gold-star cauliflower in Stardew Valley, combining prior beliefs from online sources with empirical data from Twitch streams.


This report was created by Katelyn McClure and Max Clifford for Professor Taylor Okonek.


Check out the report!
